newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Daewoo exec says still hopeful on Thomson.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo exec says still hopeful on Thomson.

text.p: South Korea's Daewoo Electronics Co is still pursuing a takeover of France's Thomson Multimedia, the unit of state-owned Thomson SA, company Vice President Nam Kwi-hyen said on Wednesday.
"Yes, we still want to take Thomson over," Nam told European businessmen in Seoul. "But we have to wait for the French government's decision."
Nam also repeated Daewoo's pledge to add 5,000 new jobs at Thomson.
"There's no reason to worry about any change in working conditions and welfare in the future," he said.
He said he believed labour unions would drop their opposition once they "see that the favourable outcome (of a Daewoo takeover) is in their best interest and the best way to secure growth".
French sources said Paris is expected to unveil this week new terms for the privatisation of electronics giant Thomson.

Last week, Paris froze its plan to sell Thomson to electronics group Lagardere for one franc. Lagardere in turn planned to sell loss-making Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo Electronics, also for one franc.
The chairman of Daewoo Electronics Bae Soon-hoon is currently in Paris, discussing the firm's determination to go through with the Thomson takeover.
Daewoo is a unit of the Daewoo Group.
